title: Programmable photonic state fusion via heralded storage of asynchronously generated resources
abstract: Probabilistic photonic sources generate elementary states in different trials, whereas multiphoton protocols require them to interfere in common temporal modes. We propose a fusion protocol that overcomes this mismatch by successively loading independently heralded photonic states into active storage loops. Conditioning on vacuum in monitored dump modes selects events in which each newly generated state is transferred into the same circulating modes as the photons already stored, thereby removing its generation time label. Provided the two alternatives of each elementary state undergo the same loading transformation, the accumulated state is described by a product of programmable linear factors, allowing a target superposition to be constructed by polynomial factorization. Adjusting the storage loop coupling as the state grows substantially improves the loading efficiency, changing the faster-than-exponential penalty of fixed balanced couplers to exponential scaling. We apply the protocol to two-photon path--frequency states for photonic clock interferometry and estimate the detected rate including source waiting time and round-trip loss.
summary: This paper details a novel photonic state fusion protocol designed to overcome the challenge of combining asynchronously generated quantum resources. By using active storage loops, the protocol effectively removes temporal labeling, enabling the construction of highly entangled, programmable NOON-type states. This advancement significantly improves the feasibility of building complex quantum devices like photonic clocks.
main_problem: The core challenge is enabling multiphoton quantum interference when the elementary photonic resources are generated probabilistically and asynchronously, requiring them to interfere in common temporal modes.
main_result: The authors propose a fusion protocol using active storage loops that successfully removes the generation time label, allowing the construction of high-fidelity, programmable NOON-type entangled states.
method: The protocol involves successively loading heralded photonic blocks into active storage loops, conditioning on vacuum modes to ensure temporal mode matching, and synthesizing the target state via polynomial factorization.
model_or_system: The system utilizes photonic state fusion, employing active quantum memory loops and heralded sources (like SPDC) to generate and combine multiple entangled photonic blocks.
key_observables: The detected rate ($R_{	ext{out},N}$) of the final entangled state, and the survival probability ($S_{N,n_b}$) of the stored state.
important_parameters: The round-trip loss ($\lambda$), the probability of obtaining a usable block ($p_h$), and the coupling strength adjustments in the storage loop.
main_assumptions: The elementary resources must undergo the same complex loading transformation for both alternatives, and the analysis often assumes ideal loss-less conditions for the final state derivation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the bosonic fusion scheme for clock-state implementation, showing process flow and mode-occupation amplitudes, and detail the source/storage architecture using SPDC sources and Bell-state analyzers.
paper_structure: The paper builds from identifying the temporal mismatch problem, proposing the storage loop loading protocol, deriving the mathematical structure of the accumulated state via polynomial factorization, and finally applying this to estimate the achievable rate for photonic clock interferometry.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses resource limitations in quantum optics, providing a scalable theoretical framework for generating high-dimensional entangled states necessary for quantum metrology and quantum computation.
